extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users who want to produce portable graphics with PGF/TikZ (students, researchers, authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Teach how to produce vector graphics in LaTeX using the PGF/TikZ system: loading packages and libraries, specifying coordinates and paths, styling lines and fills, placing nodes, using libraries (calc, intersections, patterns, snakes, layers), and plotting/animation features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package loading and libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: Using Ti k Z in a LaTeX document requires the tikz package which can be loaded by adding following command in preamble: \usepackage{tikz}. For special features special libraries must be included via \usetikzlibrary{⟨list of libraries separated by commas⟩}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \usetikzlibrary{arrow,pattern,snakes}. The tikz package also automatically loads the pgf package. A list of common libraries (arrows.meta, automata, backgrounds, calc, calendar, chains, decorations, intersections, matrix, patterns, shapes.*, snakes, spy, trees, mindmap, etc.) and brief descriptions are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: TikZ environment usage (inline vs tikzpicture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two ways to use TikZ: Inline Mode \tikz[⟨options⟩]{⟨tikz commands⟩} and the tikzpicture environment \begin{tikzpicture}[⟨options⟩] ... \end{tikzpicture}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inline mode can use baseline=<dimension> to align picture baseline with surrounding text. The tikzpicture environment encloses full drawings and accepts global picture options (e.g., scale, xscale, yscale).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate specification (Cartesian, polar, relative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinates are specified in round brackets using Cartesian (x,y), Polar (theta:radius), or relative notation ++(x,y) and +(x,y). Without specifying a unit, the standard unit is cm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1cm,2pt), (30:1cm). Relative ++(2cm,2cm) makes the last point the current position; ++ behaves differently from +. Positive x is right, positive y is up; angles measured counter-clockwise from x-axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining named coordinates and coordinates by path
rubrics_metrics.description: You can name coordinates with \coordinate (A) at (x,y); or use \path (A) ++(45:2) coordinate (B); and use \node to both place text and create a named node.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nodes and coordinates can be reused later as coordinates: \draw (x) -- (y); and anchors like (x.north) are available after defining a node.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path syntax and semicolon termination
rubrics_metrics.description: A path is specified by \path[<options>] ⟨specification⟩; and each instruction must end with a semicolon. One instruction can span several lines or include several subpaths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are shorthand variants like \draw, \fill, \filldraw, \shade, \clip, \useasboundingbox which behave equivalently to \path with the respective options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path actions: draw/fill/pattern/shade/clip/use as bounding box
rubrics_metrics.description: Options for path actions include draw, fill, pattern, shade, clip, use as bounding box (and their shorthand commands).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \path[draw] draws; \path[fill] fills the area; \path[fill,draw] fills and draws borders; \path[clip] clips subsequent drawings; \path[use as bounding box] affects picture size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric transformations as path options
rubrics_metrics.description: Geometric path options include rotate=<angle>, xshift=<length>, yshift=<length>, scale=<factor>, xscale=<factor>, yscale=<factor>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These options alter subsequent coordinates/paths within the path or scope in which they are set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color specification and opacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Colors may be specified by name or with options such as color=<color name>, draw=<line color>, fill=<fill color>, text=<text color>. Opacity is controlled by draw opacity, fill opacity, text opacity with values in [0,1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predefined colors include red, green, blue, cyan, magenta, yellow, black, gray, darkgray, lightgray, brown, lime, olive, orange, pink, purple, teal, violet, white. You can mix colors like green!20!white. pattern color=<color> sets pattern color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line width and abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Line width can be set via line width=<dimension> or abbreviations ultra thin, very thin, thin, semithick, thick, very thick, ultra thick.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviations correspond to specific point widths: ultra thin=0.1pt, very thin=0.2pt, thin=0.4pt (default), semithick=0.6pt, thick=0.8pt, very thick=1.2pt, ultra thick=1.6pt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line cap, join, rounded corners, and arrow options
rubrics_metrics.description: Options include line cap=<round|rect|butt>, line join=<round|bevel|miter>, rounded corners or rounded corners=<size>, and arrows=<start>-<end> to specify arrowheads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw[very thick, line cap=round, arrow=latex-latex, line join=round] (0,0)--(3,2); use anchors and 'arrow' or arrow tip libraries (arrows.meta) for more arrow types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line patterns and dash settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Line patterns: dash pattern=<dash pattern> (e.g., 'on 2pt off 3pt on 4pt off 4pt'), dash phase, and keywords solid, dashed, dotted, dashdotted, densely dotted, loosely dotted, double.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can fully customize dash patterns or use standard keywords for common patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using \draw to create straight line paths and closures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \draw (x1) -- (x2) -- ...; to draw straight lines; close a connected path with --cycle which connects last and first coordinates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move-to (start new subpath) is indicated by separating path segments with a space, e.g. \draw (0,0)--(2,0) (0,1)--(2,1);. Orthogonal connectors: -| and |- for horizontal-then-vertical and vertical-then-horizontal connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curved paths: Bezier, 'to' with out/in, bend options
rubrics_metrics.description: Bezier curves use '.. controls (c1) .. (c2) ..'; the 'to' operation with options [out=⟨⟩,in=⟨⟩] creates curved paths; \draw ... to[bend right] ... also creates smooth curves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax examples: \draw (0,0) .. controls (1,1) .. (4,0); \draw (0,0) to[out=90,in=180] (3,2); 'out' sets leaving angle, 'in' sets arriving angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predefined special paths: rectangle, circle, ellipse, arc, parabola, sin/cos, grid
rubrics_metrics.description: Special path commands exist: rectangle (e.g. \draw (0,0) rectangle (2,3)), circle (\draw (0,0) circle [radius=1.5];), ellipse, arc (\draw (0,0) arc (start:end:radius)), parabola, sin, cos, and grid commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show alternate syntaxes for circle/ellipse radii and rotate options. 'help lines' draws faint gray grids; \draw[step=...] grid (xmin,ymin) (xmax,ymax).

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing line appearance via options on \draw
rubrics_metrics.description: You can pass styling options directly to \draw, e.g. \draw[red, dashed, very thick, rotate=30] (1,0) -- (0,0) -- (0,1);
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine color, dash, thickness, transforms, and other options in the optional argument to change a path's appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrow tip styles and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrow tips are given with bracket notation like [->], [<->], [<<->] or more types from arrow libraries (latex, stealth, >>, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \draw[->] (0,0) -- (30:20pt); \draw[<->] (1,0) arc (180:30:10pt). Use arrows.meta library for modern arrow tip definitions; note that \usetikzlibrary{arrows} is deprecated in favor of arrows.meta.

rubrics_metrics.name: Node command and semantic: nodes are added after the path
rubrics_metrics.description: A node places text at a coordinate and is not part of the path itself. Syntax: \node[options] (Name) at (coordinates) {Text};
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nodes can be used as shapes (rectangle, circle) and styled (fill, draw, inner sep, minimum size). Nodes defined with names can be used as coordinates in further drawing commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Node options: pos, align, anchor, inner sep, outer sep, minimum size/width/height, shape aspect, fill/draw/text
rubrics_metrics.description: Node options include pos=<fraction> (position along a path), align={left|right|center}, anchor=<direction>, inner sep=, outer sep=, minimum width=, minimum height=, minimum size=, shape aspect=, fill=, draw=, text color, and sloped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: pos=.5 places text halfway; there are named pos abbreviations (at start, very near start, near start, midway, near end, very near end, at end). minimum size sets a floor to shape dimensions; size = max(minimum width, inner sep).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiline text in nodes and alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiline text uses '\\' inside node text and requires an align= option to set left/center/right alignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: node[align=left, below]{line1\\line2}. The sloped option rotates the node to be tangent to the curve when placed on a path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connecting nodes and using anchors
rubrics_metrics.description: After defining a node (x), anchors like (x.north) can be used to connect paths to specific points on the node shape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paths start at the border of a node's shape rather than the node center; you can draw arrows between named nodes like \draw (A) -- (B) or use anchors (A.north east).

rubrics_metrics.name: Placing repeated elements with \foreach
rubrics_metrics.description: The \foreach ⟨variable⟩ in {⟨list⟩} ⟨commands⟩ command allows repeated drawing operations (looping).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \foreach \x in {0,...,9} \draw (\x,0) circle (0.4); and node foreach inside a path to place shapes along a curve with node foreach \p in {0,0.25,...,1} [options] {}

rubrics_metrics.name: Clipping with \clip
rubrics_metrics.description: The \clip command removes portions of drawings outside a given shape: \clip (1,1) circle (2);
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent drawings are clipped against the current path until scope ends; useful for masking parts of drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining reusable styles (\tikzset and tikzstyle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define styles to reuse parameters: inside tikzpicture options or via \tikzset{mycircle/.style={...}} or \tikzstyle. Then apply by name in drawing commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example style definitions: mycircle/.style={circle, draw=green!60, fill=green!5, ultra thick, minimum size=7mm} and myline/.style={dotted, blue!60,->}. Use consistent naming and define styles at picture start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope environment for local transformations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \begin{scope}[<options>] ... \end{scope} to apply transformations (e.g., yshift=2cm) or styles to only part of a picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scopes localize options such as shifts, rotations, color changes, and do not affect drawings outside the scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animation in Beamer using an animatevalue variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Create simple animations in Beamer by printing multiple frames with an object shifted in N steps using \animatevalue<frames>{\p}{start}{end} and then using pos=\p/100 in node placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: define a new count variable, define the range with \animatevalue<3-10>{\p}{0}{100}, and use the variable to set node position on a path for each frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: PGF layers for ordering background/foreground
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare layers with \pgfdeclarelayer{name} and set their order with \pgfsetlayers{background,main,foreground}. Use \begin{pgfonlayer}{foreground} ... \end{pgfonlayer} to draw in a specific layer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two approaches: draw background objects first in sequence, or define layers so foreground/background can be drawn independently when coordinates depend on other layers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern library usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The patterns library defines multiple fill patterns (dots, grid, crosshatch, crosshatch dots, fivepointed stars, sixpointed stars, vertical/horizontal lines, north east/west lines, etc.) and pattern color via pattern color=<color>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Load with \usetikzlibrary{patterns} and use \draw[pattern=dots, pattern color=blue] (0,0) rectangle ++(1,1);

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake library and snake parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: The snakes library changes path structure to produce patterns like bumps, zigzag, saw, brace, coil, expanding waves, border, triangles, ticks, crosses (snake=bumps, snake=zigzag, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameters like segment amplitude, segment length, segment object length, segment angle, segment aspect, raise snake, mirror snake, line before/after/around snake, gap before/after/around snake control snake appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calc library and coordinate algebra (veclen, midpoints)
rubrics_metrics.description: The calc library (\usetikzlibrary{calc}) enables coordinate arithmetic and special functions like veclen for distance and midpoint computations using syntax such as (A) !0.5!(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \coordinate (Ap) at ($ (B) !0.5!(C) $); use let ... in ... with veclen to compute distances and draw circles at computed radii.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersection library for curve intersections
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \usetikzlibrary{intersections} and name paths with name path=<name>, then compute intersections with name intersections={of=pathA and pathB} and access intersection-1 etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw[name path=line] ...; \draw[name path=curve] ...; \draw[name intersections={of=line and curve}] (intersection-1) circle[radius=0.1]; Use 'sort by' and 'total=\t' to loop over intersections.

rubrics_metrics.name: PGF math engine and functions (\pgfmathparse, \pgfmathresult)
rubrics_metrics.description: PGF provides a math engine accessible via \pgfmathparse{⟨expr⟩} which stores a result in \pgfmathresult, and many built-in functions (add, subtract, multiply, divide, sqrt, pow, exp, ln, log10, trig functions, mod, min/max, isodd/iseven/isprime, rnd/random, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are substitute macros like \pgfmathadd{x}{y}. Constants e and pi are available. Conversion helpers rad()/deg() and angle between points/lines functions exist (\pgfmathanglebetweenpoints, \pgfmathanglebetweenlines).

rubrics_metrics.name: PGF plots: plotting functions and domain/samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot functions using \draw[domain=xmin:xmax] plot (\x,{function}); the math engine supports many functions and the trig functions assume degrees unless suffixed with 'r' for radians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \draw[domain=-2:2] plot (\x,{4-\x*\x}); use samples=50 to increase resolution; constants e and pi available; use sin(\x r) for radians.
